findings.title: Working-hours check uses `find` with inverted logic, rejecting valid slots for users with more than one availability block
findings.body: `checkIfIsAvailable` rejects a slot if `workingHours.find(...)` locates *any* working-hours entry for the slot's weekday that does not contain the slot (`start < workingHour.startTime || end > workingHour.endTime` → `return false` for the slot). `WorkingHours` is a list, and a single user routinely has several entries for the same day: a split schedule (e.g. 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00 UTC) yields two entries, and `getWorkingHours` additionally splits any schedule that crosses UTC midnight into two entries. With a 09:00-12:00 / 13:00-17:00 schedule, the 10:00 slot is inside the first entry but outside the second, so the second entry makes the function return `false` and the slot disappears. Because every user of a personal event is treated as a fixed host (`isFixed: !eventType.schedulingType`), this silently removes all slots for any user with a lunch break or a schedule spanning UTC midnight. The condition must be "no entry contains the slot" (`!workingHours.some(containsSlot)`), not "some entry does not contain the slot".

findings.title: `end` is computed from slotStartTime, so the slot end is never validated against working hours
findings.body: `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` duplicates the `start` expression instead of using `slotEndTime`. As a result the `end > workingHour.endTime` comparison can never detect a slot that overruns the end of a host's working hours. For a round-robin event where the fixed host works 09:00-12:00 and a round-robin host works 09:00-17:00, the aggregate working hours produce an 11:30 slot; for a 60-minute event it ends at 12:30, outside the fixed host's availability, yet this check passes it — exactly the over-booking of fixed hosts this PR is meant to prevent.

findings.title: Date-override check rejects slots when a date has multiple override ranges
findings.body: The `dateOverrides.find(...)` predicate returns `true` as soon as *one* override entry for the slot's date does not contain the slot, and the outer `if` then returns `false` (slot unavailable). Cal.com allows several time ranges for a single date override day, and `getUserAvailability` returns one `{start,end}` entry per range. With overrides 09:00-11:00 and 14:00-16:00 on the same date, a 09:30 slot is inside the first range but `slotEndTime.isBefore(14:00)` is true for the second range, so the slot is dropped; symmetrically the 14:30 slot is dropped by the first range. The net effect is that no slots at all are offered on days with more than one override range. The check must be "the slot is contained in none of the ranges for that date" rather than "some range does not contain the slot".

findings.title: Override containment check ignores the slot end, allowing bookings that overrun the override window
findings.body: Within the matched date override only two rejections exist: the slot ends before/at the override start, or the slot *start* is strictly after the override end. A slot that starts inside the override but finishes after it is therefore accepted: with an override of 09:00-11:00 and a 60-minute event, the 10:30 slot (ending 11:30) is reported as available. Likewise a slot starting exactly at the override end (11:00) passes because `isAfter` is not inclusive. For round-robin events this re-introduces the problem the PR fixes — the fixed host gets booked outside their date override. The condition should require `slotEndTime` to be ≤ override end (and use `isSameOrAfter` for the start comparison).

findings.title: Override date comparison mixes server-local and UTC formatting
findings.body: `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD")` builds a dayjs in the *server's local* timezone, while `slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")` is UTC (`slotStartTime = time.utc()`). On any deployment whose process timezone is not UTC the two date strings disagree near midnight, so `dateOverrideExist` is not set for the correct day: overrides are silently ignored (host booked when unavailable) or applied to the wrong day (all slots of a normal day dropped). Use `dayjs.utc(date.start)` so both sides are evaluated in the same zone.

findings.title: Dead branch: dayjs instances compared with `===`
findings.body: `if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))` compares two freshly-created objects by reference, which is always false, so this branch never executes. It was presumably meant to handle a zero-length override (a date marked completely unavailable) via `isSame()`/`valueOf()`. As written the "whole day blocked" case falls through to the generic range checks, making the behaviour accidental and hard to reason about; it also means the intent of the code is not actually implemented.

findings.title: Timezone-shifted override wraps across midnight and lands on the wrong day
findings.body: `startTime`/`endTime` are derived as `hour()*60 + minute()` after shifting the override by `inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset`, and are then applied relative to `startOfInviteeDay`. When the shift pushes the override past midnight the minute-of-day silently wraps and the override is applied to the wrong date. Example: organizer in UTC with an override 22:00-23:30 on day D, invitee in Asia/Kolkata (offset +330). The shifted time is 03:30-05:00 on D+1, giving startTime=210, which is added to the invitee's start of day D (18:30 UTC on D-1) producing slots at 22:00 UTC on D-1 — a full day earlier than the real override. In the opposite direction (negative offset crossing back over midnight) the wrap can make `endTime < startTime`, in which case `buildSlots` drops the range (`if (start >= end) continue;`) and the override produces no slots at all.

findings.title: `override.timeZone` is optional; a missing value silently uses dayjs' default timezone
findings.body: `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)` relies on the new optional `timeZone` field added to `TimeRange` in packages/types/schedule.d.ts. When a caller of `getSlots` passes date overrides without `timeZone` (the field is `timeZone?: string`), `.tz(undefined)` falls back to dayjs' default/guessed timezone (the machine's zone), so `organizerUtcOffset` is computed from an unrelated zone and the override is shifted by an arbitrary amount instead of keeping the previous UTC interpretation. Either make `timeZone` required for date overrides in this code path or default explicitly to `"UTC"`/the organizer timezone already passed into `getSlots`.

findings.title: Expensive per-slot timezone offset computation in the hot slot-filtering loop
findings.body: `checkIfIsAvailable` is invoked once per candidate slot per host (hundreds to thousands of times per `getSchedule` call on this public endpoint). For every invocation and every date override it calls `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset()` (Intl-backed, comparatively slow) and constructs ~5 additional dayjs objects, even though `utcOffset` and the converted override start/end are independent of the slot being tested. These values should be computed once per host/override before the slot loop (e.g. precomputed alongside `userAvailability`) rather than inside the predicate.

findings.title: No test covers the main fix (fixed-host date overrides in round-robin) or the new edge cases
findings.body: The only test added exercises a single-range date override for a personal event viewed from a second timezone. The headline behaviour of the PR — a fixed host's date override limiting the slots of a ROUND_ROBIN event (new `dateOverrides`/`workingHours` handling inside `checkIfIsAvailable`) — has no coverage, so the fixed-host filtering path is unverified. The new code paths that are most likely to regress are also untested: a schedule with two availability blocks on the same day (currently removes all slots, see the `workingHours.find` logic), a date with multiple override ranges, and a slot that overruns the end of an override. Adding a scenario with `hosts: [{isFixed: true,...},{isFixed: false,...}]`, `schedulingType: "ROUND_ROBIN"` and an override on the fixed host would catch these.
